title: Token Pathway Span Enrichment: cross-node per-token timing + cache-delta labels
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: instrument the request/response path to emit lightweight, structured spans for each token emission that include: node-of-execution, batch-index, prefetch/kv-cache hit/miss marker, and micro-latency buckets. These spans should be stitchable across RPC hops (frontend -> router -> worker -> cache) to allow accurate per-token latency and cost attribution even under batching, prefetch, and model-routing scenarios. This work enables: 1) chargeback and cost analytics at token granularity, 2) diagnosis of cache-delta perf regressions, 3) dashboards that show how batching and cache behavior change tail latency and unit cost.
acceptance_criteria: Span schema published and reviewed: token_span.v1 with fields (request_id, token_index, model_variant, node_id, batch_index, start_ts, end_ts, kv_cache:hit|miss|unknown, prefetched:true|false, emitted:true|false)
Instrumentation added to router and worker code paths that emits token spans without more than 50 bytes of extra payload per request on avg
Tracing backend (Jaeger/Tempo) receives stitched spans for end-to-end token paths in 95% of sampled requests
Pipeline enrichment job in metrics cluster adds cache-delta flags to token span records and emits a token_latency_timeseries metric with labels (model_variant, kv_cache) at 1m resolution
New Grafana dashboard panels showing per-token p50/p95/p99 latency by kv_cache status and batch-size breakdowns, with links to sampled traces
Unit/regression tests for span emission under batching and multi-model routing, and a load test demonstrating <5% added CPU overhead at 95th pct request rate
tasks: Design span schema and compression strategy (Ava + Marcus)
Add lightweight token-span creation API to common tracing library (ENG runtime infra)
Hook token-span creation into router before batching decision and into worker at emit-time
Propagate batch_index and node_id across RPC headers for stitchability
Annotate kv-cache code paths with cache-delta markers and expose cache policy metadata
Create enrichment job in metrics pipeline to translate spans -> timeseries and emit token_latency_timeseries metric
Add Grafana panels and alert thresholds for sudden shifts in kv_cache hit p95 latency
Run canary on a subset of serving clusters with 1% sampling for 48 hours; collect perf and cost delta
Document schema and usage in contrib/observability/token-spans.md and update runbook
telemetry_events: token_span.v1: emitted on token emission with tags: request_id, token_index, model_variant, node_id, batch_index, start_ns, end_ns, kv_cache_status, prefetch_flag
token_span_sampled.trace_id: special header used for high-detail sampling at 5x for flagged customers
token_latency_timeseries: metric emitted by aggregation job with labels model_variant, kv_cache_status, batch_size_bin
dashboard_panels: Per-token latency by kv_cache status (p50/p95/p99) - grouped by model_variant
Batch size vs per-token latency heatmap - helps isolate batching sweet-spots
KV cache hit rate and p95 delta panel - correlates cache misses with tail latency
End-to-end trace link panel - selects high p99 token spans and links into Tempo/Jaeger trace view
rollout_plan: Week 1: schema review, tracing lib change, unit tests
Week 2: instrument router and worker in staging, run synthetic workload with adjustable batch sizes
Week 3: deploy to canary cluster (10% traffic) with 1% sampling; monitor perf and errors
Week 4: widen to 50% with reduced sampling if stability good; enable metrics pipeline enrichment
Week 5: global release with dashboard made available in Console and runbook update
risks: Extra tracing payload could increase network egress and CPU—mitigated by compact schema and sampling
Stitching across RPCs depends on reliable header propagation in older router versions (may require rolling upgrades)
High-cardinality labels in metrics pipeline could increase ingestion costs if not aggregated properly
Potential GDPR considerations for storing request-level traces for certain customers (we will honor customer opt-out)
Misinterpreting cache-delta as model regression — require correlated evals before rollbacks
